items.title: Lower back pain: causes, symptoms and treatment
items.text: Everything you need to know to understand lower back pain and how to treat it effectively.
items.fullText:
Lower back pain is one of the most common complaints among adults and can develop for many reasons: poor posture, muscle overload, a sedentary lifestyle, sudden movements, stress, sports injuries or spinal problems. Although the pain is often temporary, it is advisable to seek a professional assessment if it recurs frequently or limits everyday activities.

Symptoms can range from a feeling of tension in the lower back to severe pain that makes it difficult to walk, sit or stand up. In some cases, the pain may radiate into the buttocks or legs, especially if there is nerve irritation. Stiffness, reduced mobility or a feeling of muscle weakness may also occur.

Treatment depends on the cause and how the pain develops. Physiotherapy aims to reduce inflammation, improve mobility, relax the muscles and strengthen the lower back, abdominal and pelvic areas. Patients are also taught good posture habits and personalised exercises to help prevent the problem from recurring.

Complete rest is not always advisable. In many cases, gentle, controlled activity helps speed up recovery. Walking, doing mobility exercises and avoiding sudden exertion can be beneficial. However, if the pain is very severe, or you experience loss of strength, persistent tingling or difficulty controlling your bladder or bowels, it is important to seek medical attention as soon as possible.

At Wellcare Clinics, we assess each case individually to identify the source of the pain and design a treatment plan tailored to each patient’s needs.

items.title: Tips for preventing sports injuries
items.text: Key recommendations for training safely and avoiding common injuries.
items.fullText:
Preventing sports injuries starts long before training. Preparing your body properly, allowing enough recovery time and using the right technique are key to reducing the risk of muscle discomfort, overuse problems, sprains or more serious injuries.

One of the most common mistakes is starting physical activity without warming up first. Spending a few minutes activating your muscles, mobilising your joints and gradually increasing the intensity helps your body respond better to exercise. Likewise, it is advisable to cool down after training with gentle stretches and mobility exercises.

It is also important to progress gradually. Suddenly increasing the weight, distance, speed or frequency of training can lead to overuse injuries. Your body needs to adapt gradually, especially when returning to exercise after a period of inactivity.

Technique is another essential factor. Repeating an incorrect movement many times can eventually lead to pain or injury. If you exercise regularly, it is therefore advisable to review your posture, movement patterns and exercise technique.

Rest is part of training. Sleeping well, alternating demanding training days with recovery days and listening to your body’s signals help prevent injuries. Persistent pain, excessive fatigue or a drop in performance may be signs that you need to slow down.

At Wellcare Clinics, we help athletes of all levels prevent injuries through functional assessment, physiotherapy treatment and exercise guidance tailored to their goals.

items.title: Respiratory physiotherapy: what it is and how it helps
items.text: Discover how it improves lung function and quality of life in people with a range of conditions.
items.fullText:
Respiratory physiotherapy is a branch of physiotherapy focused on improving lung function, helping clear secretions and optimising breathing patterns. It can be useful for both adults and children, particularly in cases of respiratory disease, recurrent colds, bronchitis, asthma, COPD or recovery after surgery.

Its aim is to complement medical treatment rather than replace it. Through manual techniques, breathing exercises and patient education, it seeks to improve ventilation, reduce breathlessness and help the body cope better with physical exertion.

The most common benefits include more efficient breathing, less mucus build-up, improved lung capacity and reduced fatigue during everyday activities. For patients with chronic conditions, it may also help improve quality of life and reduce the frequency of certain complications.

Sessions are adapted to each person’s age, physical condition and clinical circumstances. In some cases, patients are taught exercises to do at home, breathing control techniques and how to recognise warning signs.

Respiratory physiotherapy may be particularly advisable when there is a persistent cough, a feeling of tightness, difficulty clearing mucus or limitations when walking or climbing stairs. At Wellcare Clinics, we carry out an individual assessment to select the most suitable techniques and support the patient throughout the process.

Wellcare Clinics continues to grow with the opening of a new clinic in Madrid. This new centre aims to bring our health, physiotherapy and wellbeing services to more people, while maintaining the friendly, personalised care that defines our team.

The new clinic features spaces designed to offer comfort, privacy and a pleasant treatment experience from the very beginning. Each room has been prepared to support individual care, with modern equipment and an environment designed to make patients feel supported throughout the process.

items.fullText:
The arrival of Wellcare Clinics in Madrid is part of our commitment to offering accessible, professional, person-centred healthcare. With this new space, we aim to become a trusted destination for anyone looking to improve their health, recover from an injury or prevent future discomfort.

The centre has been designed to ensure that every patient receives comfortable, personalised care. From the initial assessment to treatment follow-up, our goal is for each person to understand what is happening, why they are experiencing pain or limitations and what steps they can take to improve.

The new clinic will provide physiotherapy treatments, therapeutic exercise, posture education and functional rehabilitation. We will also offer guidance tailored to everyday life, because we believe that a good recovery does not end on the treatment table: it continues at home, at work and in daily activities.

Our team combines experience, ongoing training and a friendly approach. We want every patient to feel heard and supported, avoiding generic treatments and focusing on solutions tailored to each case.

With this opening, we strengthen our presence and take another step in the growth of Wellcare Clinics. Madrid is opening its doors to us, and we are excited to be here.

items.title: 5 exercises to relieve back pain at home
items.text: Simple routines you can do at home to reduce pain and improve your mobility.
items.fullText:
Back pain can develop from sitting for long periods, lifting heavy objects, sleeping in an awkward position or performing repetitive movements. Although each case should be assessed individually, there are gentle exercises that can help reduce tension and improve mobility.

The first recommended exercise is a lower back mobility exercise on the floor. Lie on your back with your knees bent and slowly move your legs from side to side without forcing the movement. This helps relax the lower back.

The second exercise is the cat–cow stretch. Start on all fours, gently arch your back upwards, then lower your abdomen while slightly raising your head. Move slowly and with control.

The third exercise involves bringing one knee to your chest. Lying on your back, draw one knee towards your chest and hold the position for a few seconds. Then switch legs. This exercise can relieve tension in the lower back and buttocks.

The fourth exercise is the glute bridge. With your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor, slowly lift your pelvis and lower it again. This helps safely activate the glutes and lower back.

The fifth exercise is diaphragmatic breathing. Place one hand on your abdomen and breathe deeply, aiming to let your abdomen rise as you breathe in. Breathing more effectively can help reduce muscle tension.

These exercises should be performed without severe pain. If any position worsens your symptoms, it is best to stop. At Wellcare Clinics, we can help you find the most suitable exercises for your situation.

items.title: The importance of good posture in everyday life
items.text: Small habits that make a difference to your health and help prevent injuries.
items.fullText:
Posture directly influences how our muscles and joints function throughout the day. Spending many hours sitting, looking at your phone with your neck bent, working at a computer without good ergonomics or lifting objects incorrectly can cause back, neck or shoulder pain, as well as headaches.

Good posture does not mean staying rigid all the time. In fact, the body needs movement. What matters is avoiding awkward positions for long periods and learning to distribute loads more evenly. Changing position frequently, getting up regularly and doing short mobility exercises can make a big difference.

At work, it is advisable to adjust your chair height, keep your feet firmly on the floor and position your screen at eye level. If you use a laptop for many hours, a stand and an external keyboard and mouse can help prevent neck strain.

When using your phone, try holding it a little higher instead of constantly lowering your head. During household activities such as cleaning or lifting objects, it is advisable to bend your knees, keep the load close to your body and avoid sudden twisting movements.

Strengthening your muscles is also important. A strong back, active core muscles and good mobility help you maintain better posture without excessive effort.

At Wellcare Clinics, we provide personalised posture education, helping each patient improve their daily habits and prevent future discomfort.

items.title: Orthopaedics
items.text: Diagnosis and treatment of musculoskeletal injuries, sports injuries and traumatic injuries.
items.fullText:
Our orthopaedics service focuses on the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of injuries affecting the musculoskeletal system. We treat problems involving muscles, joints, bones, tendons and ligaments, adapting treatment to each patient’s needs.

We carry out an individual assessment to identify the source of the injury and determine the most appropriate treatment. We work with sports injuries, joint problems, fractures, muscle overload and other conditions that may restrict movement or cause pain.

Our aim is to help you reduce discomfort, regain mobility and gradually return to your usual activities safely.

items.imageAlt: Illustration of the pelvis and lower back
items.title: Rehabilitation
items.text: Functional recovery and restoration of movement after surgery or injury.
items.fullText:
Rehabilitation aims to gradually restore mobility, strength and function after an injury, surgery or a prolonged period of inactivity.

Every recovery process is different, so we carry out an initial assessment to set realistic goals and design a programme adapted to each patient’s progress.

During treatment, we may combine manual therapy, therapeutic exercise, mobility work and strengthening exercises to promote a safe recovery and help patients regain their independence in everyday activities.

items.title: Specialist physiotherapy
items.text: Advanced physiotherapy: pelvic floor treatment, sports physiotherapy, invasive physiotherapy, respiratory physiotherapy and manual lymphatic drainage.
items.fullText:
Specialist physiotherapy addresses a range of conditions through treatments adapted to each person’s individual characteristics and needs.

We begin with an individual assessment to understand the source of the discomfort, any existing limitations and the patient’s goals. We then select the most suitable techniques and exercises to improve mobility, reduce pain and restore function.

Our approach combines treatment, exercise and education so that patients can take an active role in their recovery and maintain their results in the long term.
